title: Algorithmic bias: where it comes from and how to recognise it

videos.script: Panela's marketing team likes the churn model of lesson 17 so much that they want a second use for it. A loyalty club, with free delivery, for the customers the model calls safe: a risk below 0.2. {{proposal}} Before that goes ahead, somebody should ask a question the model's overall numbers cannot answer. Is it wrong about everybody equally? {{question}} It is not. A loyal customer in the North, one who keeps ordering, is flagged as a likely leaver more than twice as often as a loyal customer anywhere else. Under the club, that customer is shut out for being loyal at a distance. {{finding}} And the model never saw anybody's region. Region was not one of its inputs. {{no-region}} This lesson is about how that happens. Where bias in a model comes from, how an audit finds it, and why the same error can be a gift under one decision and a closed door under another. {{end}}
